features.title: ablation_blocks support under LoRA (configure_lora_params / inject_lora_cross_attention)
features.user_visible_behavior: --ablation_blocks N restricts which of the 16 SpatialTransformer blocks get LoRA adapters (blocks[N-1:], same convention as the pre-existing full-DP-SGD configure_dp_params path), instead of being silently ignored under --use_lora as it was before.
verification: py_compile src/Model/lora.py src/Model/Diffusion/LDM_dp.py src/LDM_dp_finetune.py src/LDM_dp_inference.py
./init.sh -- confirm the smoke-test checkpoint (ablation_blocks=-1 in its saved args) still logs '16/16 SpatialTransformer block(s)' (regression check: old checkpoints/behavior unchanged).
Direct unit check: inject_lora_cross_attention(unet, ablation_blocks=N) for N in [-1,1,8,16,20] and confirm blocks-injected / lora-param-tensor counts match blocks[N-1:] semantics.
evidence: 2026-08-11: ablation_blocks=-1 -> 16/16 blocks, 256 lora tensors; =1 -> 16/16 (same); =8 -> 9/16, 144 tensors; =16 -> 1/16, 16 tensors; =20 -> 0/16, 0 tensors (out-of-range, degrades to empty -- configure_lora_params/configure_dp_params both raise RuntimeError on an empty param list, so this fails loudly rather than silently training nothing).

./init.sh rerun post-change: existing lr2e-3_eps10 checkpoint (ablation_blocks=-1) generated identically, log read '16/16 SpatialTransformer block(s) (ablation_blocks=-1, ...)' -- confirms backward compatibility.
features.notes: Previously --ablation_blocks was only consumed by configure_dp_params (the non-LoRA path) -- it had ZERO effect whenever --use_lora was set (true for every checkpoint trained so far, including the eval-LI-* and eval-plain-eps10 entries below). LDM_dp_inference.py's build_and_load_ldm now also reads ablation_blocks back out of a checkpoint's saved args and re-applies the same injection range at inference time, for both the adapter-only ('lora' key) and full-checkpoint-with-embedded-lora ('model' key) load paths.

features.title: LDM training-objective research: min-SNR loss reweighting + auxiliary XRV classifier-guidance loss, DP-budget-free (multi-angle analysis + implementation + pilot A/B)
features.user_visible_behavior: Follow-up to experiment-synth-utility-pretrained-fullreal's finding that every downstream-classifier-SIDE lever failed to rescue synthetic-only training, shifting suspicion to the LDM checkpoints' own generative fidelity. This feature adds two opt-in (off-by-default, fully backward-compatible) research levers to LDM_dp_finetune.py's training objective, grounded in a multi-angle analysis of the existing DP-SGD fine-tuning code: (1) --min_snr_gamma (Hang et al. 2023 min-SNR-gamma loss reweighting, eps-parameterization only, zero architecture risk), (2) --cls_loss_weight (an auxiliary BCE loss between a frozen TorchXRayVision classifier's prediction on a VAE-decoded x0 estimate and the study's real CheXpert label, gated to low/mid timesteps via --cls_loss_max_t). Both are folded into the SAME per-sample backward pass Opacus already clips+noises, so they add ZERO extra DP-budget cost (privacy accounting depends only on target_epsilon/target_delta/sample_rate/epochs, not loss function shape -- verified empirically in the smoke test, see evidence). Other analyzed-but-deferred proposals (x0-parameterization switch, multi-hot label-embedding conditioning, partial ResBlock/GroupNorm unfreezing) are documented in the analysis but NOT implemented this round -- each has a specific structural risk (e.g. x0-parameterization needs the frozen output layer unfrozen too, or it trains against a target the frozen weights can't represent) that makes them unsuitable for a first pass.
verification: py_compile / ast.parse clean on src/Data/mimic_cxr.py, src/Model/Diffusion/ddpm.py, src/Model/Diffusion/LDM.py, src/Model/Diffusion/LDM_dp.py, src/LDM_dp_finetune.py after the changes

smoke test A (regression): tiny 32-train/8-validate manifest, 1 epoch, ALL NEW FLAGS OFF -- confirms byte-for-byte-equivalent code path still completes cleanly (exit 0, same eps_spent/sigma as before the refactor)

smoke test B (new path): same tiny manifest, --min_snr_gamma 5.0 --cls_loss_weight 0.1 --cls_loss_max_t 300 --log_every 1 -- confirms the classifier loads once (lazy), the timestep gate actually gates (loss_cls only appears in step logs when that step's t < cls_loss_max_t), loss values stay finite, AND privacy accounting (sigma, final eps_spent) is IDENTICAL to smoke test A given the same steps/epochs/target_epsilon -- confirms the 'no DP-budget cost' claim empirically, not just by code inspection

pilot A/B: two real DP-SGD LoRA fine-tunes from the same --pretrained_ckpt (ldm_epoch0100.pt), same 2,000-image train subset (data_manifests/mimic_p10_p12/pilot_lossresearch_manifest.csv.gz, seed=42) + full 802-image validate split, same target_epsilon=10/epochs=8/seed=42 -- 'baseline' (all new flags off) vs 'clsloss' (min_snr_gamma=5.0, cls_loss_weight=0.2, cls_loss_max_t=300) -- compare train/val loss curves, then generate+evaluate a small image set from each resulting LoRA checkpoint against the existing eval pipeline (clip_label zero-shot AUROC + a quick downstream_cls XRV-NIH label-agreement pass) to see whether the new loss objective measurably changes label-relevant fidelity in the DIRECTION goal 2/3 of the prior session need.
evidence: 2026-09-07: multi-angle analysis grounded in the actual code (not just literature): current setup is plain eps-parameterization simple-MSE loss (original_elbo_weight=0 by default, so VLB term contributes nothing), uniform timestep weighting, cross-attention-only trainable (ResBlock/conv backbone + final output layer fully frozen even under full DP-SGD, let alone LoRA), text-only conditioning via BioBERT->cross-attention (the UNet's ADM-style single-class label_emb pathway exists but is disabled/unused and doesn't support multi-label anyway). Key grounding fact: Opacus privacy accounting (compute_noise_multiplier) depends ONLY on (target_epsilon, target_delta, sample_rate, epochs) -- NOT on loss function shape -- so any new loss term folded into the same backward pass is DP-budget-free.

2026-09-07: implemented --min_snr_gamma in ddpm.py/LDM.py (per-timestep loss weight min(SNR(t),gamma)/SNR(t), eps-parameterization only, None=off=identical to prior behavior) and --cls_loss_weight/--cls_loss_max_t/--cls_loss_xrv_weights in LDM_dp.py (auxiliary BCE loss reusing Eval_metric/downstream_cls.py's load_xrv_classifier/XRV_TO_CHEXPERT -- no duplicate CheXpert-label-mapping logic -- defaulting to the '-nih' XRV weight set specifically to avoid any dependency on this private dataset possibly being in a '-all'-style classifier's own training data). Refactored LDM.py's p_losses into _diffusion_forward + _loss_from_model_output so LatentDiffusionDP.p_losses can add the auxiliary term reusing the SAME UNet forward pass (no duplicate forward, no risk to Opacus's per-sample-grad hooks from a second forward call). Extended Data/mimic_cxr.py with an opt-in return_chexpert_vector flag (3-tuple __getitem__ instead of 2-tuple, default False = every existing caller unaffected) to expose raw CheXpert label vectors needed by the auxiliary loss.

2026-09-07: smoke tests A and B both passed on a real GPU under real Opacus DP-SGD wrapping (not just static analysis) -- see verification. Notably: smoke test B's per-step log showed loss_cls appearing only on the ONE of three logical steps whose Poisson-sampled t happened to land under cls_loss_max_t=300, confirming the gate works; both smoke tests produced eps_spent=8.9212 with sigma=0.6628 given identical (target_epsilon=10, epochs=1, steps=3) -- empirical confirmation of zero DP-budget cost.

2026-09-07: launched a real pilot A/B (not just a smoke test) -- 'baseline' (cuda:0) vs 'clsloss' (cuda:1), 1,858-image train subset (2,000 sampled, 142 dropped for no positive CheXpert label) + full 748-image validate subset (802 sampled, 54 dropped), target_epsilon=10, epochs=8, LoRA, seed=42 identical otherwise -- finetune_dp/pilot_lossresearch/{baseline,clsloss}/. In progress; results to be added once training completes and a small generate+eval pass is run on both resulting checkpoints.
features.notes: Session request (2026-09-07): explain the concrete next-step plan BEFORE executing, and analyze the LDM training method/loss from multiple angles (e.g. adding a classifier term, switching the loss target from noise-prediction to x0-prediction) with concrete improvement proposals. Working in git worktree .claude/worktrees/synth-utility-improve (branch worktree-synth-utility-improve). Deferred-but-documented proposals for a LATER round: (a) x0-parameterization switch -- risky as-is, since only cross-attention is trainable and the final UNet output layer stays frozen, so there's no trainable layer positioned to adapt to a changed loss target; would need to also unfreeze/adapt the output layer first. (b) multi-hot label embedding conditioning via the UNet's existing-but-disabled num_classes/label_emb pathway -- likely needs a non-private warm-start/pretraining stage before a short DP fine-tune can use it meaningfully (use_scale_shift_norm=False means this would be a brand-new additive signal the frozen ResBlocks were never trained to interpret). (c) partial ResBlock/GroupNorm-affine unfreezing, mirroring the existing ablation_blocks pattern -- directly addresses the hypothesis that cross-attention-only fine-tuning can't fix pixel/texture-level classification-relevant fidelity, but needs its own small-scale validation round before committing GPU-time to a full run.
